items.title: Bitcoin Caught in Inflation Crossfire
points: U.S. consumer prices rose 0.4% in October, beating forecasts for the third consecutive month, pushing Bitcoin below $73,000 and triggering $589 million in liquidated long positions (forced closures of bets that an asset's price will rise) in 24 hours.

Fed Governor Christopher Waller said a 50 basis point rate hike (a move raising borrowing costs by half a percentage point, double the typical increase) should be considered if core inflation hits 0.3%, which it did.
Traders now assign only 12.8% probability to that aggressive hike (up from zero the day before), with a quarter-point increase still the consensus for the Fed's December 9 decision.
Spot Bitcoin ETFs (exchange-traded funds tracking Bitcoin's price) continue seeing net outflows, adding to selling pressure ahead of the Fed's move.

items.title: Anthropic Moves Toward Public Markets
points: Anthropic set its IPO price range at $70–$78 per share, valuing the Claude AI developer at up to $1.4 trillion on a fully diluted basis (including all potential shares from options and conversion rights).
The company plans to begin trading under ticker 'ANT' on November 19, backed by $26 billion in private investment commitments from Nvidia, Google, and other tech firms.
Decrypt's prediction market now gives Anthropic a 97% probability of going public before the end of 2026, up from 71% a week earlier.

items.title: Security and Regulatory Risks Emerging
points: Binance flagged an Apple iOS flaw called 'worse_query' that could expose users' private keys (cryptographic codes needed to access digital assets); Apple has not publicly confirmed it.

Senator Elizabeth Warren, set to chair the Senate Banking Committee, is signaling 'tough questions' for prediction markets and Trump-affiliated crypto businesses, with an aide telling the Trump family to 'preserve documents.'
A shareholder class action lawsuit accuses Nvidia and CEO Jensen Huang of failing to disclose alleged national security risks tied to the CEO's personal relationships.

items.title: Miami-Dade Bitcoin Tax Payments
points: Miami-Dade County, Florida's largest county by population, now accepts bitcoin for property tax payments both online and in person.
This marks one of the largest U.S. government jurisdictions to formally accept bitcoin for tax revenue, setting a precedent for other municipalities.

items.title: Trump Media's Q3 Bitcoin Acquisition
points: Trump Media purchased a net 1,510 bitcoin for $112 million during Q3 2026, treating it as a long-term treasury asset rather than a trading position.
The move signals institutional-level confidence in bitcoin as a store of value among major U.S. corporations.

issues.subject: 👀 Miami-Dade Now Accepts Bitcoin for Taxes

headlines: Miami-Dade County now accepts bitcoin for property tax payments both online and in person, marking a major U.S. government adoption milestone.
Trump Media purchased a net 1,510 bitcoin worth $112 million during Q3, signaling major corporate treasury allocation to cryptocurrency.

sections.title: Miami-Dade Bitcoin Tax Payments
points: Miami-Dade County, Florida's largest county by population, added bitcoin as an accepted payment method for property taxes.
Payments can be made online and in person, making cryptocurrency a practical option for residents' tax obligations.
This represents one of the largest U.S. government jurisdictions to formally accept bitcoin for tax revenue, setting a precedent for other municipalities.

sections.title: Trump Media's Q3 Bitcoin Acquisition
points: Trump Media purchased 1,510 bitcoin net during the third quarter of 2026, spending $112 million total.
This move represents a significant corporate treasury strategy, with the company treating bitcoin as a long-term asset rather than a trading position.
The acquisition signals institutional-level confidence in bitcoin's role as a store of value among major U.S. corporations.
